runs.text: has m rows and n columns over a field F;
represents m linear equations in n unknowns.
Swapping two rows, scaling a row by a nonzero scalar, and adding a multiple of one row to another preserve the solution set of an augmented system.
Gaussian elimination reduces [A|b] to echelon form; continuing to the unique reduced row echelon form exposes pivot and free variables.
For square A, the following are equivalent: A is invertible, every column is a pivot column, Ax=0 has only the zero solution, and Ax=b has exactly one solution for every b.

items.text: All entries and row operations are taken over one fixed field F; a row may be scaled only by a nonzero field element.
The product AB is defined only when the number of columns of A equals the number of rows of B.
A left or right inverse need not imply a two-sided inverse for arbitrary rectangular matrices; the equivalence above is for square matrices.

items.text: Row operations preserve the solution set but generally change eigenvalues and determinants.
Matrix multiplication is associative but usually not commutative.
